subject.title: acp: assistant text corrupted when Gateway revises in-progress output (non-append revision mis-sliced)

question: How should the ACP bridge represent Gateway `replace: true` revisions when standard ACP message chunks cannot retract already-emitted text?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but the obvious full-text re-emit can still be wrong for append-only ACP clients, so maintainer intent is needed before changing streaming semantics.

options.title: Choose conservative ACP mapping
options.body: Buffer or otherwise avoid unretractable provisional output when Gateway replacement semantics are possible, then add text and thinking regression tests.

options.title: Use a client capability or extension
options.body: Adopt a replace-aware ACP extension only if maintainers are willing to document fallback behavior for clients that ignore it.

options.title: Accept corrected follow-up output
options.body: Emit the replacement as a new message and accept that some clients may show both stale and corrected text.

recommendation.title: Choose conservative ACP mapping
recommendation.body: Buffer or otherwise avoid unretractable provisional output when Gateway replacement semantics are possible, then add text and thinking regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans ACP product behavior and the original ACP bridge ownership trail points most strongly to steipete.
